spots.s: The Mother Church — do the daytime tour, but a night show in those pews beats any arena on earth.
Two blocks of gold records, Elvis's Cadillac and rotating exhibits that go way beyond country — pair with a Hatch Show Print tour.
The longest-running radio show on the planet — snag a backstage tour or just take the show; someone surprising always drops in.
A full-scale Parthenon with a 42-ft golden Athena inside — absurd, gorgeous, and the lawn around it is prime picnic-date turf.
Walk the honky-tonk strip once at night just for the neon and the bands pouring out of every door — free, loud, and unmistakably Nashville.
Golden-hour skyline shots from a 1909 truss bridge — the easiest impressive date-walk downtown has.
The What Lifts You wings mural, record shops and rooftop patios in Nashville's slickest few blocks.
I Believe in Nashville mural, Draper James, Five Daughters biscuit-donuts — an easy afternoon loop that always fills a first date.
A 1930s mansion on 55 acres of botanical gardens with seasonal light shows — the single most reliable date venue in the city.
Otters, herons and zero traffic noise eight miles from downtown — the lake loop is the city's best head-clearing walk.
Climb the iconic limestone staircase off Belle Meade Blvd, then loop the ridgeline — Nashville's classic sweat-then-brunch move.
Preserved Victorian main street 30-some minutes south — bookshops, whiskey bars and the Franklin Theatre marquee; strong date-afternoon energy.

spots.n: Nashville Sounds at First Horizon Park
spots.s: Triple-A baseball under the guitar scoreboard in Germantown — cheap seats, good beer, zero pressure; ideal easy date or solo night.
Jack White's lacquer-yellow HQ — browse the vault and cut your own record in the 1947 Voice-o-Graph booth (date gold).
Blockbuster rotating exhibitions inside a stunning art-deco post office — Friday evenings stay open late.

spots.n: National Museum of African American Music
spots.s: Fifty genres from gospel to hip-hop with interactive mixing booths — the best museum hour on Broadway, hands down.
Free, huge and quietly excellent — from Mississippian artifacts to civil-rights Nashville; pairs with the farmers' market next door.
Year-round produce sheds plus an international food hall by Bicentennial Mall — Saturday-morning ritual material.
The 7th president's mansion and grounds 20 minutes east — unvarnished history done seriously; good out-of-town-guest card.
A 1900s auto factory turned warren of makers — Antique Archaeology, Corsair distillery tastings and Grinder's Switch studios.
Kix Brooks' hillside winery with free Music in the Vines sets Sat & Sun — pack a picnic, grab a bottle, watch the sunset.
Craft cocktails, all-day kitchen and six reclaimed bowling lanes — the do-everything first-date hedge that always works.
Nine acres of jungle under glass with an indoor river — free to wander, kitschy-spectacular, and clutch on a rainy day.
Civil War fort ruins with a wide-open skyline view — free, quiet, and ten minutes from Broadway.

nightlife.n: The Spot by Dre and Snoop
nightlife.s: Dre & Snoop's Still G.I.N. den in the 2nd Ave catacombs — plush booths, heavyweight sound and DJs running G-funk through trap till 3a weekends.
Tennessee's biggest LGBTQ+ dance floor — resident DJs, drag between sets, zero attitude; voted the city's best place to dance for a reason.
The one Broadway multi-level worth your night: skip the band floor, head up to the DJ level when it flips to hip-hop, finish on the rooftop.
Four floors at Broadway's river end — Fri/Sat rooftop DJ dance parties with Cumberland views are the least-country move on the strip.
Black-owned Dickerson Pike hideout — proper cocktails, DJs leaning R&B and hip-hop, intimate enough to actually talk.
Velvet 300-cap room off Music Row — Analog Soul nights (hosted by Lovenoise) are Nashville's best R&B hang.
Home of Motown Monday (9p, free) — GQ called it the most stylish party in America; soul and funk 45s keep the floor packed till late.
East Side's beloved 'Beast' — and the frequent landing pad for The Boom Bap, the long-running old-school hip-hop DJ round robin.
A 1948 Printers Alley basement: live jazz nightly and an 11p burlesque revue Thu–Sun — the date-night power move downtown.

nightlife.n: Bourbon Street Blues and Boogie Bar
nightlife.s: Printers Alley's New Orleans corner — blues and funk bands grinding into the small hours since 1996.
The real honky-tonk: Brazilbilly on stage, a $6 fried-bologna Recession Special, and locals who can actually two-step.
Robert's scrappier next-door neighbor — no cover, tight bands, and room to dance if you claim the floor early.
Midtown's music-industry hang — live bands late, a rowdy dance-adjacent crowd, and doors that stay open till 3a.
A cinderblock time capsule in the Gulch where bluegrass royalty still drops in — get in line early, sit anywhere, be amazed.

nightlife.n: The Blue Room at Third Man Records
nightlife.s: Third Man's intimate venue side — live shows, guest-DJ dance nights and 16mm screenings, open to the public Thu–Sat.
Germantown's bowling-lanes-meets-concert-hall — catch a tour you actually care about with a lane and fried chicken on the side.
The Dolly-pink rooftop atop the Graduate — frozen drinks, skyline views and maximum date energy; dress a little.
Gatsby-ish room off Printers Alley with virtuoso bluegrass and western swing nightly at 8 — dinner-and-a-show without the tourist tax.
Karaoke in a double-wide trailer run by Santa himself — cash only, $2 beers, and the friendliest room of strangers in town.

eats.s: The 14-seat, 14-course, $75 East Side omakase Nashville waited years for — OpenTable seats drop at midnight, six weeks out.
A 60-minute, 12-course $65 edomae sprint inside Dream Nashville off Printers Alley — velvet, gold and a great pre-Alley launch pad.
Germantown's sleek fish temple — pristine nigiri and a $140 chef's tasting Sun–Thu when you want to swing big.
The Gulch's dressed-up sushi stalwart since 2000 — Chef Himmi's nigiri and robata skewers still earn the scene.
Nashville's OG Japanese spot on White Bridge Rd — honest sushi, tempura and a proper Japanese grocery next door; no reservations, lines move.
Elliston Place standby for solid rolls without the scene — daily 4–6p happy hour keeps it cheap.
East Nashville's izakaya — yakitori off the binchotan, tonkotsu ramen and sake flights; a Charlotte Ave outpost is on the way.
The Gulch original that taught Nashville ramen — 12-hour broths, counter seats, in and out happy.
A tiny 12South heavyweight — duck dumplings and kakigori that landed on every national best-of list; go early, share everything.
Charlotte Pike's chef-run grill-and-broth hall — private rooms, real banchan, and ventilation that saves your jacket.
No-frills Charlotte Pike institution — bibimbap and soondubu like somebody's mom is in the kitchen, because she is.
Arnold Myint's revival of his mother's legendary Belmont steam table — Thai comfort plates at student prices.
Berry Hill's bright pho-and-banh-mi shop — clean flavors, fast counter service, reliable solo lunch.
Husband-and-wife Gallatin Ave shop stacking the city's best banh mi — grab two, hit Shelby Park.

chinese.s: No sign — look for the giant red strawberry on Meridian St; chili-cumin brisket noodles and crispy guo tie worth the first-come line.
Hand-pulled Chongqing xiaomian and Szechuan chili chicken on Belcourt — the closest thing to a Chengdu noodle shop in town.
Hillsboro Village's xiao long bao specialist — bamboo steamers, scallion pancakes and boba two doors from the Belcourt.

chinese.n: Sichuan Hot Pot & Asian Cuisine 蜀香园
chinese.s: Tennessee's first big Sichuan hotpot hall, out Nolensville Pike — order the mala broth and the full Sichuan menu nobody translates.
Green Hills' old-guard Cantonese room — weekend dim sum service with har gow, siu mai and char siu bao done properly.
Cool Springs' broth-bar hot pot with a legit dim sum list — worth the drive south when the craving hits on a weeknight.
The Charlotte Pike institution since 1995 — wok greens, a live-fish counter and every chili bean paste Sichuan cooking needs.

chinese.n: CAAN Chinese New Year Celebration 春节
chinese.s: Free lion dances, calligraphy and dumplings at Centennial Park every February — Feb 6 2027 rings in the Year of the Fire Goat.

chinese.n: Cumberland River Dragon Boat Festival 龙舟节
chinese.s: Twenty-paddler dragon boats race the Cumberland downtown every fall — free to watch from Riverfront, and rookie teams are welcome.

fishing.n: Percy Priest Lake — Elm Hill Marina
fishing.s: Largemouth, hybrids and slab crappie 25 minutes out — biggest rental fleet in town plus live bait and TN licenses right at the dock.
Free bank and kayak-launch access on Priest's quiet west shore — work the rocky points at dawn before the ski boats wake up.

fishing.n: Old Hickory Lake — Sanders Ferry Park
fishing.s: Hendersonville's big-water playground — bass on the riprap, stripers pushing bait, and plenty of bank to roam.
When the generators roll, stripers and monster skipjack stack in the churn below the dam — heavy jigs, heavier leaders.
Catfish and the odd freight-train striper ten minutes from Broadway — ramp and long riverbank inside the park.

THE destination trip: ~220k stocked rainbows and browns below Center Hill Dam — check the generation schedule before wading Happy Hollow or Betty's Island, and carry the TN license plus the $22 trout add-on.
A stocked 60-acre TWRA lake in the Joelton hills — pier, ramp and electric-only quiet; buy the small daily lake permit online first.
No-gas-motor lake with an accessible fishing pier and a paved 2-mile loop — sight-fish bass and bream on calm mornings.
Float the 5-mile Bell's Bend loop at the Narrows for scrappy smallmouth — Kingston Springs outfitters run canoes and shuttles all season.

fishing.n: Lake Acorn & Creech Hollow (Montgomery Bell SP)
fishing.s: Two small, calm lakes in the Dickson County hills — 26-acre Acorn and 17.5-acre Creech Hollow — for largemouth, channel cats, crappie, bluegill and redear; bass size limits are strict and posted, and a TN license is needed from age 13.

A quiet Gallatin arm of 22,500-acre Old Hickory Lake known for bass, crappie, catfish and sauger — two launch ramps, decent bank fishing along the lakeside trails, and a wetland zone that's off-limits to anglers.

biking.s: 11 miles of rocky, punchy lakeside singletrack 25 minutes out — Lakeside loop for warm-up, Pinnacle when you mean it; closes when wet.
Nine flowy miles hugging Old Hickory Lake in Gallatin — jump line, rock-garden drop, and the region's best-maintained dirt.
Nine beginner-to-intermediate machine-built miles in southeast Davidson — the confidence-builder before Hamilton Creek humbles you.
A ~20-mile backcountry loop through thick Dickson County forest — the area's biggest single ride, 40 minutes west.
Flat, fast paved miles along the Cumberland — cross the river on the greenway bridge and ride all the way to Percy Priest Dam.
Farmland doubletrack and gravel loops in a Cumberland oxbow 20 minutes out — zero traffic, big-sky quiet.
Roll south from the northern terminus over the double-arch bridge — low-traffic parkway climbing, then biscuits at Loveless as the reward.

About 8 miles of intermediate singletrack packed into a small Columbia park, with the most challenging sections up the hill — locals call it some of the best riding in Middle Tennessee. Free, night riding allowed; bring water.
Rocky, rooty singletrack in four nested loops (the longest 4.5 miles), with a switchbacked, bouldery climb to Bald Knob and a fast, loose descent back off it. Take it slow the first lap.
Murfreesboro's 9-mile network of beginner-through-advanced singletrack loops in a big city park — an easy add-on for a day in Rutherford County.

social.s: The icon: free 4–6 miles from 11th & Holly with pace groups for every speed, ending at 3 Crow Bar — the easiest fifty new friends in Nashville.
Free lesson at 7:15 then an open floor of salsa and bachata till midnight — no partner needed, friendliest Latin night in town.

social.n: Salsa & Bachata Mondays at Nashville Palace
social.s: Early-evening salsa and bachata by the Opry — beginner-friendly floor that beats another Monday on the couch.
The legendary Post 82 party, now at Eastside Bowl — free two-step lesson at 7, The Cowpokes at 8, and everybody dances with everybody.
Volunteer-run nonprofit swing studio on Woodland St — Friday lesson then hours of lindy hop with a crowd that rotates partners by default.

social.n: Swingin' Tuesdays at Global Education Center
social.s: All-levels lindy, balboa and charleston night on Charlotte Ave — cheap, welcoming, and nobody sits out long.
The city's pro jazz jam in a Gleaves St listening room — players sit in, everyone else gets world-class music at neighbor distance.
Sign up online at 11a Monday for a shot at the most famous 90 seconds in songwriting — or just take a seat and watch legends-in-waiting.
Hundreds of pickers jamming under the barn lights in Percy Warner Park — bring an instrument or a lawn chair; either way you'll talk to strangers.
Free multi-genre shows on the Centennial Park lawn with food trucks and dogs everywhere — the lowest-stakes social scene in the city.
East Nashville coffee-and-beer cafe with a free 500-game lending library — pull up to an open table and you're mid-conversation in minutes.
Fridays from 11:30a with Nashville Basketball Opportunities at Nashville First Church of the Nazarene · $3 on Meetup.

social.n: Indoor Soccer at Shelby Community Center
social.s: The game takes place at Shelby Community Center(East Nashville). Tuesdays from 6p with Nashville soccer at Shelby Ave at S. 20th - At entrance of Shelby Park near Tennis Courts, Nashville · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Weekly Indoor Climbs on Friday - Climb West
social.s: We are meeting at Climb West every Friday at 6pm for indoor climbing. First time pass or daily pass includes all rental equipment needed to climb. Fridays from 6p with Climbing People of Nashville at Climb Nashville West · no Meetup fee.
The other team and subs can watch from the trail. Mondays from 6p with Nashville soccer at Coleman Park Community Center, Nashville · no Meetup fee.
Wednesdays from 11:30a with Nashville Basketball Opportunities at Nashville First Church of the Nazarene · no Meetup fee.
Wednesdays from 6p with Tennis Nashville Meetup at Hillwood High School, Nashville · no Meetup fee.

Class + Prática will be held weekly with Shelby and the NZ team from 12pm-2pm. Class will range from 1 hour to 1.5 hours. Sundays from 12p with Salsa Nashville at Global Education Center, Nashville · no Meetup fee.
Tuesdays from 8:30a with Tennis Nashville Meetup at Richland Park, Nashville · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Mossy Ridge Trail - Evening Hike for Experienced hikers (Bring a Light!)
social.s: Tuesdays from 6p with Nashville Hiking Meetup at Percy Warner Park - Deep Well Entrance, Nashville · no Meetup fee.

social.n: 8v8 Soccer Match Co-Ed @ International Indoor Soccer Complex
social.s: Mondays from 8p with Nashville Pick-Up Soccer Meetup Group at International Indoor Soccer, Antioch · $13.99 on Meetup.

social.n: Open Board Games and Card Games Night
social.s: Play board and card games at this twice weekly event, open to gamers of all levels of experience -- feel free to drop in! Wednesdays & Fridays from 5p with Nashville Area Gamer Association - NAGA at Cheshire Hall, Nashville · no Meetup fee.

remote.s: Downtown at 159 4th Ave N (Suite 100). Phone booths, an unlimited coffee & tea bar and stocked café, copy/print and 24/7 member access. Meeting rooms are $65/hr and event space $350/hr.
remote.p: $15 day pass · $69 day office · $199/mo community · offices from $499/mo

remote.s: Third floor of Gulch Crossing, 1033 Demonbreun St. Privacy booths, a kitchen with snacks, showers, bike storage and outdoor space. Guests are registered ahead and show photo ID at the building door. Day passes run M–F 9a–5p, on-street parking and garages nearby. Industrious also has Nashville spaces in Germantown (Neuhoff), Downtown and Nashville Yards.

Coworking at 1131 4th Ave S (#230) in Wedgewood-Houston. High-speed Wi-Fi, complimentary coffee & tea, privacy booths, a library, a printer, videoconferencing in the meeting rooms and on-site parking. M–F 8a–7p.
remote.p: Day pass from $50 · coworking from $395/mo · meeting rooms from $70/hr
remote.b: Quiet, focused floor, per member reviews

remote.s: Coworking inside the Kenect residential building at 800 19th Ave S, Midtown, near Music Row and Vanderbilt; you buy a day pass online. Fast internet, printing & scanning, meeting rooms, private phone booths, pet-friendly office pods and a community kitchen. Mon–Fri 9a–6p, Sat 10–5, Sun 12–4.
remote.p: Day pass ≈$25 · Float, Dock & Pod memberships

remote.s: Suite 1000 at 1801 West End Ave, Midtown. Coffee & tea, privacy booths, a kitchen, a printer, A/V and whiteboards; monthly plans bundle utilities, cleaning, printing and refreshments into one price. M–F 9a–5p; on-street parking, with garages within a mile.
remote.p: Day pass from $35 · meeting rooms from $75/hr

remote.s: Main Library at 615 Church St, downtown. Free Wi-Fi, group study and meeting rooms bookable online, printing and mobile printing, color copies, a laptop vending machine, Studio NPL and the Robinson Courtyard. From Nov 2, 2026, park at Nashville City Center (220 6th Ave N) for $4.99 for up to 4 hr: scan the QR codes in the garage and by the first-floor desk. Mon–Fri 9–6, Sat 9–5, Sun 2–5.
remote.b: Quiet study areas; weekdays calmer than weekends

remote.s: East Nashville's branch at 206 N 11th St. Wi-Fi, meeting rooms bookable online, printing and mobile printing, public computers, Studio NPL and free parking. Mon/Wed/Fri 10–6, Tue/Thu 12–8, Sat 10–5; closed Sun.

West-side branch at 720 Baugh Rd in Bellevue. Wi-Fi, group study rooms, printing and mobile printing, public computers, a community garden, and free parking with EV chargers. Mon–Thu 10–8, Fri 10–6, Sat 10–5, Sun 2–5.

Frothy Monkey's bungalow café at 2509 12th Ave S in 12South. Nashville Guru singles out its two-top tables for remote workers and students; the all-day menu runs from coffee and brunch to mains, greens and grain bowls, with a bar for later. Open daily 7a–8p.
remote.b: Busy on weekends, with long coffee waits; plenty of indoor and patio seats

remote.s: Nonprofit coffee shop and roaster at 424 Humphreys St in Wedgewood-Houston, with lots of natural light that Nashville Guru calls a great work environment, soft seating and a pleasant back patio. Flat whites on the house espresso and the Sunny Hunny (honey, almond, cardamom); sales fund programs for teens.
remote.b: Seats are first-come, so arrive early; weekdays quieter

remote.s: 8th & Roast's café at 2108 8th Ave S in Melrose, from Nashville roasters working since 2009: community tables, bar seating and a calm room. Every syrup and cold foam is made in-house, and the bakery covers gluten-free and vegan options. Open every day 7a–6p (the Charlotte Ave café keeps the same hours).
remote.b: Compact room, lively but not chaotic; go off-peak for calm

events.n: A Country Christmas at Gaylord Opryland
events.s: The 43rd edition fills the resort: ICE! carves Home Alone out of two million pounds of ice, alongside a new cirque show, ice tubing and the Delta riverboat cruise. Book ICE! tickets online ahead.
Two arena nights at Bridgestone, with Devon Again opening.
Nashville Ballet's hometown Nutcracker with the Nashville Symphony in the pit, at TPAC's Jackson Hall.
Holiday editions of the Opry on select nights at 7p in the Opry House: country stars, Christmas classics and a multi-artist lineup every night.

events.n: Victoria Monét: Frequency of Love Tour
events.s: The Grammy-winning R&B singer plays The Truth in Wedgewood-Houston.
The '90s R&B group celebrates 35 years of Forever My Lady at The Truth. It's a grown-and-sexy slow-jam night.

events.n: Christmas at the Ryman (Amy Grant & Vince Gill)
events.s: The 16th annual holiday residency, 12 shows in the Mother Church, with 3p matinees added on Dec 19, 20, 22 and 23. Buy only through ryman.com, because tickets are non-transferable.
An AFC South rivalry game at Nissan Stadium, a noon kickoff. Walk the pedestrian bridge over from Lower Broadway.
A Saturday-night holiday game that closes the Preds' 2026 home slate, across from the Broadway honky-tonks.

events.n: New Year's Eve Live: Nashville's Big Bash
events.s: A free concert at Bicentennial Capitol Mall with Little Big Town, HARDY and The Red Clay Strays, broadcast nationally on CBS, with more acts still to be announced. Gates open at 5:30p.
Two arena nights of the bluegrass phenom at Bridgestone. A ticket to either night is required to request seats for the Feb 21 Ryman finale.
A world-premiere Cinderella with the Nashville Symphony, at TPAC's Jackson Hall.
Two nights of clean, food-obsessed stand-up from Jim Gaffigan on his Everything Is Wonderful tour at the Ryman Auditorium.
An AFC South Sunday on the East Bank as the Titans host Jacksonville at Nissan Stadium, a walk across the pedestrian bridge from Lower Broadway.
The comedian, rapper and actor brings his stand-up to The Truth, the new Live Nation hall in Wedgewood-Houston.
Cheekwood's gardens and mansion glow on a timed-entry evening walk, entries every 30 minutes from 4:30p; closed Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day.
Pittsburgh visits Bridgestone Arena for a Saturday-evening Preds game steps from the Lower Broadway honky-tonks.
Nashville's long-running holiday gift market fills the Fairgrounds with hundreds of vendors for one weekend — handmade gifts, décor and seasonal treats.
The zoo's after-dark holiday light walk, nightly 5–9p, with illuminated trails and Santa visits on select nights through Christmas Eve.
The gospel and R&B hitmaker brings his choir-powered show to Live Nation's new 4,400-cap Wedgewood-Houston venue.

events.n: Trans-Siberian Orchestra: The Ghosts of Christmas Eve
events.s: TSO's 30th-anniversary winter tour — rock-orchestra holiday spectacle with lasers, pyro and a full string section at Bridgestone Arena.
Free downtown holiday market by Walk of Fame Park over two long weekends (Dec 3–6 and 10–13), with local makers, food and a tree lighting.
Nashville Repertory Theatre stages the Disney musical in TPAC's Polk Theater, Thursday–Sunday across three weekends.
SEC vs. Big Ten bowl game at Nissan Stadium, 2p CT kickoff on ESPN — one of the last big games in the current stadium.

events.n: A Beautiful Noise: The Neil Diamond Musical
events.s: The Broadway tour of the Neil Diamond bio-musical plays TPAC's Jackson Hall for a one-week run.

Our Cuban Salsa class provides you with an opportunity to learn the authentic form of this circular style of Cuban dancing called Casino! Sunday from 2:30p with Salsa Nashville at Casa Azafrán (Global Education Center Studio), Nashville · no Meetup fee.

Join the Nashville Tennis Club on November 17 from 6–8 PM for a fun outdoor on-court hitting session! Great rallies, rotating partners, and new faces to meet. Come play, connect, and bring the energy! Tuesday from 6p with Nashville Tennis Club at Centennial Sportsplex, Nashville · no Meetup fee.

Join the Nashville Nerd Herd for a night of brain-teasing trivia! Whether you're a trivia master or just looking for a good time, this event is perfect for all levels of knowledge! Sunday from 7p with Nashville Nerd Herd at HONEYTREE MEADERY, nashville · no Meetup fee.

events.n: A Gleeful Meeple Game Night @ Homegrown Taproom
events.s: For those new to Gleeful Meeple Events: GM Nashville is an all-inclusive social gaming (tabletop, outdoor, trivia, etc.) community created to help people in Nashville make friends and support local businesses. Wednesday from 6p with Gleeful Meeple: Play Games, Meet People at Homegrown Taproom & Kitchen, Nashville · no Meetup fee.

iceskating.s: The Predators' twin-rink in South Nashville, open since 2014. Public skates are booked online only through a DASH account and the building is cashless: matinees $10.98 and evenings $13.73 plus tax, rental skates included. Cancel at least 24 hours ahead for a refund.

The Predators' west-side twin rink, opened in 2019, with a full-service bar and restaurant, a Pure Hockey shop and a dek hockey rink next door. Public skate pricing matches the other Ford rinks (matinee $10.98, evening $13.73, skates included), and sessions are booked online in advance.

The Metro-owned rink at Centennial Sportsplex near Centennial Park, the Predators' practice ice since 1998 and now run by a team affiliate under a deal that runs through 2049. Phased upgrades to locker rooms, glass and the ice plant are planned. Public skates can be booked online or paid at the rink.

The newest Predators rink, opened in July 2023 beside F&M Bank Arena in downtown Clarksville; the drive makes sense when a Nashville session is sold out. It's open as late as 11p Tue–Thu, and public skates book online at the same cashless rates as the Nashville rinks.

Nashville Yards' holiday rink under the Broadway viaduct downtown, upgraded to real ice for 2026 and opening Nov 21 as part of Holiday Central (through Jan 3). Tickets weren't on sale yet in early November; parking is $15 for three hours in the West Garage via the Metropolis app.

A 9,000 sq ft outdoor rink of real ice in the resort's Pinetop Village, open Nov 8, 2026–Jan 2, 2027 as part of A Country Christmas. One ticket covers unlimited skating all day on its date; rent skates or bring your own. Tickets are online only and priced by date, parking is extra, and kids 11 and under need a ticketed adult on the ice.

The Predators-presented outdoor rink inside the zoo's Glow Wild light show, nightly Nov 13–Jan 3 with gates at 5p. Skating is a $12 add-on ($10 members) to Glow Wild admission and buys a 45-minute session with rentals. Above 50°F the rink may close, with refunds. Weekday openings are the quietest.

Murfreesboro's outdoor rink at The Fountains at Gateway, open Nov 20, 2026–Jan 31, 2027. Admission covers tax, skate rentals and 120 minutes on the ice: $20 for 13+, $15 for ages 4–12, and free for 3 and under with a paid adult. A light drizzle doesn't stop skating; heavy rain can shut it briefly. Groups of 20+ book a day ahead.

skating.s: The paved spine of Shelby Bottoms runs about 4.5 miles one way along the Cumberland through a 950-acre floodplain preserve in East Nashville, and riders call it flat, smooth and shaded. Side trails are gravel or dirt, and the ramp up to the river pedestrian bridge is steep, so plan your turnaround.

Nearly 10 miles of asphalt from the Cumberland past the Two Rivers skatepark to Percy Priest Dam. Some reviewers find it smooth with few bumps; others warn of a couple of steep hills and tree-root cracks, and a 2024 review reported the boardwalk section closed. It gets crowded near the trailheads.

A 9-mile asphalt path from Ted Rhodes Park along the Cumberland's west bank into downtown's Riverfront Park, crossing the Shelby Street Bridge to the stadium side. Reviewers call it smooth and flat but industrial, set back behind a water plant for long stretches, and often nearly empty.

Four disconnected paved segments along the Harpeth in Bellevue, 9.1 miles in all, including a loop through Bellevue Park on a bend of the river. Reviewers call it a very smooth ride apart from worn blacktop near Edwin Warner Park; a bridge closure was reported in July 2025. Light, unhurried traffic.

Six separate paved segments through Whitsett, Ezell, Antioch, Orchard Bend and Mill Creek parks in southeast Nashville, 9.8 miles in all. TrailLink lists it for inline skating; the pieces don't connect, so pick one park's stretch for laps. It's near Ford Ice Center Antioch for a two-rink day.

Brentwood's 14.75 miles of asphalt link Tower Park, Smith Park, the library, the YMCA and the city's ball fields, and the city lists roller-blading among the intended uses. Suburban and park-bound, it suits shorter loops rather than a long out-and-back; park at any of the trailside parks.

Murfreesboro's 12-ft-wide asphalt greenway runs about 10 miles along the Stones River and Lytle Creek past Civil War sites, with a spur to the national battlefield. An inline skater gave it 3 of 5: few root cracks, but roughly half is coarse aggregate that buzzes through your wheels.
